LOCALISATION: West Papua | HJ22+CQH Nehibe, Jayapura Regency, Papua
CHARAC_LVL1: Rock art site / Petroglyph / Pictograph / Hand stencil
COMMENTS: Description: Sukun Stone is a number of stones of various sizes and shapes that are arranged in an area of 2,60 metres x 2,60 metres. These stones consist of a mother stone in the form of a monolith shaped like a diamond or a parallelogram with an uneven surface. In addition, there is a menhir statue with an oval head shape and wearing a tapered head and a circular headband on the forehead. On his oval face, there is a rope tie on the edge of the face from the forehead to the chin. His eyes and nose are worn out so they are invisible, his ears wear wavy earrings that jump up to his shoulders, the tip of his chin is long to his chest and covers his neck. The chest of the statue is not identified, but it seems to be using clothes because on the arm there are grooves like dangling cloth. His waist is wearing a waistband. On the genital part, there is a triangle shape, at the bottom there is a boundary in the form of a circular line, while on the side and back of the statue there are grooves of clothes that fall like fabric grooves under the neck and waist. The shape of the leg is unknown because the condition of the lower part is tapered, maybe because it is worn out or it is. Another possibility is because the position of the statue in the past was not on his back or sleeping on the ground, but was stuck standing on the ground. According to the community, this statue is a girl (Merawai) who is the source of the sukun fruit. Besides this, there are eight oval-shaped menhirs with smooth surfaces arranged transversely on the ground surface with a west-north-south east orientation. There is also a stone plate (betew) that has been broken and the broken part is gone. On the remaining stone plates, three oval-shaped basins appear on the surface. One of the basins is still intact, while the other two basins are partially left because they are broken. The stone plate functions as a place for offerings. | Keywords: papua, west papua | Alternative_Name: Batu Sukun

LOCALISATION: West Papua | Meukisi, Yokari, Jayapura Regency, Papua 99354
CHARAC_LVL1: Rock art site / Petroglyph / Pictograph / Hand stencil
COMMENTS: Description: Lingkar Stone (oru dia ) is a number of monoliths arranged in a circle. The arranged stones are generally round, oval, and flat with a smooth surface. The Ring Stone is in the yard of Ondoafi's house or the chiefs according to their respective roles in the custom. The Ring Stone Formation consists of eight stones, ten stones, eleven stones, and twelve stones. According to the community, the number of stones on each ring stone should be twelve according to the number of their descendants, and the middle part is a place to make fire. At this time, from a number of Lingkaryang Stones, some have been found that are arranged on the ground without protective buildings and some have also been given protective buildings. There is also a Ring Stone that has been cast so that it cannot be moved. Lingkardi Stone functions as a seat during customary deliberation. However, at this time in some areas of Batu Lingkar there are benches that are arranged in a circle for seating and the existence of Batu Lingkar is only as a symbol. As a place of deliberation, usually if a meeting is going to be held, it is given a code or sign by lighting a fireplace in the middle of the Ring Stone. The ring stones are in accordance with their function divided into two, namely for peaceful tribal groups who talk about the problems of daily life of indigenous people, both related to economy, socio-culture, health, and welfare. War tribal groups specialise in discussing war issues. In every village where there is a Lingkar Stone. The number of Ring Stones for a peaceful tribe is more than for a war tribe which is only one. | Keywords: papua, west papua | Alternative_Name: Batu Lingkar

CHARAC_LVL1: Rock art site / Petroglyph / Pictograph / Hand stencil
COMMENTS: Description: The 'Tungku Api' Fire Furnace is a burning furnace located in the middle of a traditional meeting place. This furnace is in the shape of a circle of an array of stones that rising and the centre is filled with soil and ash from burning as well as a fireplace that is still burning. In the area around the furnace, there are long benches arranged around the furnace as seats during the deliberation. Fire in the furnace must die and must be kept alive. This is related to trust thanks to life and the presence of immortal figures (Wari). COMMENTS: The research by the Archaeology Center of Jayapura in 2010 reported that prehistoric rock artworks were found on this coral reef island with vegetation in the center of the island, while the exterior of the island consisted of steep cliffs with niches right above the seawater surface. COMMENTS: Description: Rock art: These paintings were inscribed on stone surface with scratch technique, there is some are painted singly and some are in pairs one boulder consists of 2 to 5 painting in the direction facing the painting is sufficient varies. The rock paintings are comprehensive into 4 fenced sectors and 3 sectors that have not yet been ring-fenced The total number of painting motifs is 147 paintings etched on chunks 115 stones. Stone chiselled figures (Pahatan Batu): At the Tutari megalithic site in sector IV there are several stones carved to resemble a creature carved to resemble a a creature consisting of a head, neck and body. These stones are believed to be the leaders of the cursed Tutari tribe, meanwhile the condition of some of these stones has begun eroded until it has its shape and size not the same anymore. Stone Rows (Jajaran Batu): Represent an arrangement of two rows of stones (The right row consists of 70 stones and the row on the left consists of 44 pieces stone) with the base oriented towards groups of painted stones and sections the tip leads to a group of menhirs. Models of megalithic remains like this are common associated with a ceremony activity. Stone Enclosure (Batu Temu Gelang): It is an arrangement of stones that are arranged circular one end to the other meet. the number of existing stones about 6 groups and is in a painted stone complex. As for form The arrangement of the temugelang stones is quite varied. Menhirs (Batu Tegak): On the peak of the Tutari hill it is found quite a lot of menhirs of that size varies, starting from the smallest size 14 em to the largest size of 88 em. There are a total of 110 groups of menhirs with its own uniqueness, namely that the menhirs are located at megalithic sites Tutari is not embedded into the ground however only erected supported by stones small so it doesn't collapse (Prasetyo, 1994). | Keywords: papua, west papua

COMMENTS: At this site, two excavation boxes were opened. The first was opened on the top of the hill, to the north-east of the second box. The human remains sampled for isotopic analysis were found in the second unit and included Ymk/1-R (radius) and Ymk/2-P (phalange), which were selected for collagen stable isotope analysis. Ymk/1-R was found at 54 cm below the surface associated with molluscs and pottery fragments. The sediment associated with this depth was dark brown in colour with grain size ranging between 2 and 0.02 mm, reflecting sandy loam. Ymk/2-P was found associated with pottery fragments at 135 cm depth, in a sediment with grain size ranging from 0.02 to 0.002 mm. One radiocarbon determination is available for this site, based on charcoal that dates to 2590±120 BP (Suroto 2016, 1). The charcoal was found in the same spit as Ymk/2-P, providing an approximate age for the specimen. No radiocarbon dating has yet been obtained for the upper spits associated with Ymk/1-R, but it can be assumed that this specimen postdates 2590±120 BP.
